article.title: Hindi to English: Shopping context
article.description: Hindi: 'क्या आपके पास इसका बड़ा साइज़ है?' English: 'Do you have this in a bigger size?' Teaching point: natural English phrasing avoids literally translating 'बड़ा साइज़' as 'big size' — native speakers say 'a bigger size' or 'a larger size'.
article.content: Hindi: 'क्या आपके पास इसका बड़ा साइज़ है?' English: 'Do you have this in a bigger size?' Teaching point: natural English phrasing avoids literally translating 'बड़ा साइज़' as 'big size' — native speakers say 'a bigger size' or 'a larger size'.

generated.caption:
Ever tried asking for a 'big size' in a shop and felt something was off? 🤔

In English, when you ask for a different size, we usually say 'a bigger size' or 'a larger size'. Avoid literally translating 'बड़ा साइज़' as 'big size' – it sounds much more natural this way!

For example: 'Do you have this in a bigger size?'

slides.headlineRest: — The Right Way to Ask in English
slides.body: When shopping, the Hindi phrase 'क्या आपके पास इसका बड़ा साइज़ है?' is used to ask for a larger garment. However, a direct translation like 'Do you have this in a big size?' sounds less natural to native English speakers. The correct and commonly used phrasing is 'Do you have this in a bigger size?' You can also use 'Do you have this in a larger size?' Remember to use the comparative form 'bigger' or 'larger' when referring to an item that's bigger than the one you're holding.
